props.label: Main
props.html:
Commercial window cleaning in Melbourne

Commercial glass, on a cycle rather than a request

Shopfronts, offices, showrooms, entries and internal glazed partitions across Melbourne. The cleaning is straightforward. What makes commercial glass work is being there before you open, on a frequency that is already agreed, so nobody has to notice and nobody has to approve it.

  • Before opening or after close
  • Weekly through to quarterly
  • One scope, one invoice, across sites
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Windows, gutters, roof and solar
  4. Commercial window cleaning

What you are actually buying

Not a window clean. A frequency. Commercial glass does not have a clean state and a dirty state, it has a rate at which it degrades, and the only real decision is how far down that curve you let it go before someone turns up.

That is why this is sold as a schedule. A shopfront cleaned fortnightly never looks dirty to a customer and takes fifteen minutes a visit. The same shopfront cleaned when somebody finally complains takes an hour, has already cost you the impression, and has to be re-approved every time. The second version is more expensive in every way that matters.

How often

By what the site actually is

Starting points rather than rules. Exposure, traffic and how close you are to a main road move all of them.

What we would normally propose, and what drives it.
  Suggested frequency Why
Retail shopfront Fortnightly to monthly It is the first thing every customer sees and it collects hand marks daily
Hospitality, cafe and restaurant Weekly to fortnightly Glass near food service marks fastest, and alfresco glazing takes weather
Office tower lobby and entry Weekly High traffic, high visibility, and the part tenants judge the building by
Office floors, external glass Quarterly Exposure driven rather than traffic driven
Car showroom Weekly The entire proposition is looking at things through glass
Medical and professional rooms Monthly Perception of cleanliness matters more here than almost anywhere
Warehouse and industrial office Quarterly to twice yearly Low public visibility, dust driven rather than traffic driven
Body corporate common glazing Quarterly Entry doors, lobbies and stairwell glass, usually on the same cycle as the common property clean

Swipe for the rest of the columns

What makes it work

Four things, none of which are about glass

Out of hours by default

Retail before opening, hospitality after close, offices at weekends or early morning. Quoted at the time it will actually be done rather than quoted at day rate and surcharged afterwards.

Approved once

An agreed scope at an agreed frequency, costed per visit. It happens without anyone raising a job, and you get a record of each attendance for the file.

Site requirements sorted first

Inductions, insurance documentation, access cards, alarm codes and permits are arranged before the first visit, not discovered at the door.

One contact across sites

Multi site retail or a portfolio runs as one scope with one invoice rather than a booking per address, which is where the admin cost actually sits.

In a commercial glass visit

Standard, every attendance.

  • External glazing at ground and accessible upper levels
  • Entry doors, including both faces, push plates and frames
  • Internal glazed partitions and reception glass where included in the scope
  • Frames, sills and tracks rather than glass alone
  • Fingerprints and hand marks on doors, which are what people actually notice
  • Cobwebs cleared from frames, awnings and signage surrounds
  • A record of the attendance for your file

Quoted separately

Related work that is genuinely a different job.

  • Multi storey and high rise glazing. High rise window cleaning
  • Elevated work platform hire where a site has no safe access
  • Signage and illuminated sign faces. Sign cleaning
  • Facade and panel washing above the glass line. Commercial building washing
  • Hard water and construction deposit removal, which is restoration rather than cleaning
  • Anti graffiti film supply and fitting on repeatedly targeted shopfronts
  • Internal high level glazing requiring a scissor lift inside the tenancy

Questions

From facilities and store managers

Can you come before we open?

For retail and hospitality that is the default rather than an option. Nobody wants a bucket and a squeegee in front of their shopfront at eleven on a Saturday.

Offices are usually early morning or weekends. The time is agreed when the schedule is set up and it does not change without you knowing.

How do you handle access and keys?

However your site requires. Most external work needs no access at all. For internal glass we work with whatever arrangement you already have: a key safe, a building manager, a security escort or an alarm code.

We will not improvise an access arrangement. If it is not agreed, we do the external work and tell you.

Do we have to approve each visit?

No, and that is the point of a schedule. The scope and the frequency are approved once and costed per visit, so the work happens on the cycle without anyone raising a job each time.

You get an attendance record for each visit, which is what most facilities teams and committees actually need.

What if the glass has hard water spots or construction film?

Then it is not a cleaning job, it is a restoration one, and it is quoted separately. Mineral deposit from sprinklers and alkaline film from a nearby build both bond to glass and need treatment rather than washing.

Left too long, both etch the glass permanently and the only fix is replacement, which is why it is worth dealing with early. Hard water and mineral stains.

Do you do multi site retail?

Yes, and it works considerably better as one arrangement than as a booking per store. One scope, one frequency, one contact and one invoice, with a per-site rate so the cost is predictable.

It also means a store manager does not have to find a window cleaner.

Can you do the windows and the rest of the exterior together?

That is usually the sensible arrangement. Glazing on a short cycle, entries and footpath on a medium one, hardstand and facade annually, all under one scheduled maintenance agreement rather than four separate relationships.
